hypothesis: Absolute integer final-margin modeling improves exact-line/key-number probability calibration
validation_scheme: nested season walk-forward; per-game seven-offset evaluation
feature_set: market fair margin; optional total; actual integer home margin
model: normal lattice baseline; spread-conditioned discrete; spread+total discrete
secondary_metrics: 3-class log loss; closing-line Brier; non-push binary Brier; push calibration; key-number diagnostics
result: Normal Brier 0.515859 vs spread-discrete 0.517467; normal-minus-discrete -0.001606, 95% CI [-0.003717,+0.000573]. Integer push calibration improved 3.103% to 3.778% vs 4.020% observed; at 3 predicted 8.079% vs 9.613% observed and at 7 predicted 5.662% vs 4.825% observed.
decision: REJECT FULL DISCRETE REPLACEMENT; RETAIN KEY-NUMBER SIGNAL
notes: Full empirical cover/loss replacement worsened aggregate Brier, but absolute-margin modeling fixed the 0006A structural QA failure and materially improved key-number push mass. Total did not earn incremental weight. Advance a targeted hybrid push correction.
